title: P3 — полный Perplexity research prompt и follow-ups

sections.title: Research-only scope
sections.text: Владелец поручил углубить D26/D27/D28 с опытом cloud/OSS систем и подготовить полную передачу для новой сессии. Prompt — исходящий research document, не принятие recommendations и не новый design gate.

sections.title: Prompt отправленный в Perplexity Deep Research
sections.text:
ROLE: Independent research architect. Research established production patterns for Vaulter's P3 design. Do not rubber-stamp the provisional A/A/A decisions. Challenge the framing, propose a better third option when evidence warrants, and clearly distinguish documented facts, analogy/inference, and your design recommendation. Produce the answer in Russian, preserving technical identifiers. Cite primary-source URLs near each substantive claim. Prioritize vendor official documentation, standards, and maintained open-source documentation or pinned source code; blogs only as leads. Check current behavior at retrieval time; note version/edition and exclusions. Do not infer proprietary internals from user-facing help pages. Report unknowns rather than inventing Google Drive behavior.

SYSTEM CONTEXT (repository-confirmed, not hypothetical):
Vaulter is an unpublished MIT PHP/Laravel modular file/document platform being designed for 1.0. No external consumer backwards compatibility is required, but database history and stored user data must be preserved. PHP ^8.4, Illuminate/Laravel supported ^12|^13; current local Laravel13.17, Pest4.7.4/PHPUnit12.5. It is an embeddable package suite, not a hosted AWS clone: core, drive, media, documents, Filament adapter, Azgard authorization adapter. Optional TipTap/Yjs collaboration and later Vue/REST integration. Core must not depend on optional drive/documents packages.
Canonical API Vaulter::drive(owner)->actingAs(user)->nodes()/folders()/files()/trash()/access()/shares()/activity(); explicit asSystem(nonempty reason). Immutable handles, no cached access decisions. Operations re-fetch passed node models by persisted key within authoritative drive/tenant; passed actorId/model fields are not authority. User View denial→404 concealment; ability denial→403; profile deny→ProfileRestriction403. Accepted narrow TOCTOU window: ACL prechecked outside SQL, structural/tenant invariants rechecked under lock. Public share fresh read after revoke commit→404; already delivered bytes cannot be revoked.
Runtime profiles are frozen core policies per drive: feature booleans/global AND profile; max size min; MIME allow predicates AND; blocked extensions union; required scan global OR profile. Per-profile permission drivers provide ACL; configured host drivers can allow ACL but shouldn't implicitly create tenant authority. Current proposal system bypasses ACL only; scope/profile/quarantine remain.
Strict tenant isolation applies also to system/queues. withoutTenancy is closure-scoped maintenance exception with finally restoration; not an HTTP input. Jobs carry scalar actor/drive/revision/blob/tenant IDs, rehydrate authority, and avoid worker tenant leakage.
Content: tree of folder/file/document/shortcut nodes; immutable file revision history; CAS blobs with tenant/drive/global deduplication scope, references determine liveness, transactional edge/quota updates, race-safe asynchronous GC/reconcile. Storage backends local or S3-compatible. A scan verdict is currently planned on a revision rather than automatically authoritative globally by sha. Avoid cross-tenant information leakage or unqualified global clean sharing.
Single/PHP/tus/S3 multipart completion converge on real-byte ingest, bounded stream reads (~64KiB), size/hash/MIME trusted only after actual reading. SQL retry reuses staged bytes, no second CAS. Completion result pointers committed atomically; replay creates no duplicate revision/event/job. Jobs currently specified after OUTERMOST SQL commit. No built-in mandatory AV vendor or cloud deployment.
Status model proposed scan_status=not_required|pending|clean|infected|failed; metadata remains ACL-visible in quarantine. Pending/failed block all byte egress when scan required, infected blocks always, clean permits. Every egress must gate before stream/signed URL/preview/export/thumbnail/public share/cache; no silent older-clean-head substitution. Old revision explicit read has its own verdict.
Historical upgrade fills existing revisions with not_required. New ingest when scan optional uses not_required, required uses pending+scan. Copy/restore inherit status; currently pending/failed new revisions get their own idempotent scan job after outermost commit, clean/infected/not_required inherited.
Purge is atomic per subtree with physical node deletion and document inline revision FK cascade; bulk maintenance isolates/report errors by root and continues. Copy unsupported document kinds fails before any subtree writes; no empty payload.
Concurrency: separate advisory/row lock families ordered session→tree→node→file→revision→quota→CAS→event writes. Optimistic expectedSequence compared under node lock before any side effects; successful mutation +1 within same DB transaction, no-op no bump. Idempotency key is separate from sequence, blob hash separate from ETag.
Project phases: P0/P1/P2 closed; P3 authorized PHP API/security/profiles/upload/quarantine/tenancy; P4 document aggregate/lifecycle; P5 domain event/outbox integration; P6 REST. P3 public API already promises expectedSequence/StaleNodeException412, but existing governance assigned creation of v_nodes.sequence to P4.7. Current repair moves only foundation to P3.3, P4.7 extends new Document writers/REST ETag contract (REST activation P6).
We are doing RESEARCH ONLY now. No product implementation, accepted decisions, independent audit, or phase closure. Next session will finalize design. Three questions remain OPEN. Current provisional choices must be tested against evidence.

QUESTION 1 — scanner policy vs legacy/copy/restore content (D26/F05/F04):
A currently proposed: not_required remains readable unconditionally after required is enabled, preserving legacy availability; new required ingest scans.
B: require clean for all reads after required enabled, block legacy and introduce explicit rescan/backfill.
Find established alternatives: separate scan fact from enforcement policy; modes off/new-uploads-only/all-content; explicit grandfathering; policy epoch/scanner version/signature freshness; scan verdict keyed by revision vs immutable object version/blob digest with scope; background backfill with explicit cutover/rollout; failure/unsupported/too-large/password-protected states; fail-open/closed handling. Explain if A silently weakens 'required' and if B needlessly breaks availability. For unpublished software what should the default mean? Should policy choice be explicit rather than an opaque not_required exception? Who controls it? What semantics should copy or restore have when source not_required but destination requires scan? Distinguish same-content/same-scope copy, cross-drive/profile/tenant copy, same hash but new object version, clean result under changed scanner/policy, infected inheritance, stale verdict, quarantine effects of a scanner outage.
Use Amazon GuardDuty Malware Protection for S3 (event-driven new objects vs on-demand existing objects, tags and IAM/TBAC, outcomes/failures/copy metadata/events), Azure Defender for Storage (on-upload/on-demand scanning, existing blob behavior, access gating/private endpoints, result trust), Google Drive documented malware limits/download restrictions (not claims about internal AV), Nextcloud/files_antivirus and other maintained OSS as appropriate. If an on-demand feature is newer distinguish it and mark historical/outdated pages. Explicitly assess event delivery gaps, afterCommit isn't a durable dispatch guarantee, crash after commit before queue publish, idempotence vs at-least-once durability; existing outbox in repo is not automatic P3 adoption. Signed URLs may survive app revocation/status changes: identify achievable contract vs exact storage enforcement, TTL and version pinning. Do not expand into enterprise AV deployment; propose minimum adequate portable core and deliberate extensions.
Deliver a full access matrix for status × effective scan mode incl legacy, scanner outage, copy/restore/destination requirements and specific counterexample tests.

QUESTION 2 — system actor and non-bypassable policy (D27/F06):
A: system bypasses object ACL only, profile/tenant/quarantine/invariants remain enforced.
B: early system-return also bypasses profile restrictions.
Compare AWS IAM permissions boundaries/SCP/resource policies (explicit deny and documented root/service-linked-role exceptions), Google Shared Drive restrictions vs service accounts/domain-wide delegation vs actual administrator actions, Azure/RBAC if relevant, OSS service-account/system-job patterns, OPA/Cedar capabilities/principal/context models.
Do NOT equate our in-process trusted system actor with an IAM principal without stating limits. Categorize actor identity, object ACL, resource/business feature policy, security scan, data invariants, tenant scope, maintenance capabilities. Decide which are inviolable and which may need narrowly scoped admin/recovery exemptions. Evaluate broad asSystem vs explicit service principal/capabilities/reason/audit; avoid a generic bypassPolicy flag. Does a profile disabling uploads/downloads/shares accidentally prevent purge/repair? What exact policy applies to deletion/cleanup of infected files? Can maintenance jobs progress without public data egress? Where does break-glass belong if at all in MVP? Give guard order/error semantics, owner binding (P3.1 seam→P3.6 policy implementation), system/user/maintenance tests.

QUESTION 3 — optimistic concurrency and sequence foundation timing (D28/F08):
A: sequence column/locked compare+bump in P3.3 to satisfy promised PHP API, later Document writers and REST ETag use it.
B: postpone to P4.7 and redesign earlier API contract.
Compare established Google Drive revision/version semantics (is version a useful precondition? do not assume files.update supports If-Match from generic HTTP), Google Cloud Storage generation/metageneration preconditions, S3 conditional requests/If-Match and distinction ETag vs hash/multipart/versionId, Azure Blob ETag concurrency, Nextcloud WebDAV conditional updates, HTTP RFC9110 conditional requests/strong vs weak ETag.
Define what node sequence counts and which writers must participate: name, parent, trash/restore, content replacement, grants/shares/profile/child-list changes/scan status, revision pruning and asynchronous verdict updates. Distinguish node metadata revision from file content version and collection/list version; a strong ETag must change for all representation changes and authorization-dependent representations may complicate caching. Avoid exposing untrusted sequence int from caller/model as authoritative. Ensure two expected7 writers produce one success8/one412 with no side effects; optional expectedSequence vs mandatory protocol precondition, retries safe/no blind retry after stale; batch/subtree multiple-node semantics, rollback/idempotency, create/copy initial0. Single column vs multiple counters and portable unsigned semantics PostgreSQL/MySQL. Assess whether broad 'all mutations' wording is underspecified and whether stage foundation early with ownership amendment is the only compilable honest option.
Recommend minimum correct P3 version scope and P4/P6 contracts without overengineering.

OUTPUT:
1. Summary recommendation for each D26/D27/D28, including rejection/revision of current A choices if needed, reasoning, tradeoffs, and evidence strength.
2. Comparison table by system (documented feature, limits, what applies to Vaulter, what does not); at least 2 genuinely relevant primary-source anchors per question, no manufactured parity.
3. Separate scan fact/enforcement and system privilege/concurrency models with concrete state/access/copy/restore/error tables.
4. 10–20 adversarial acceptance scenarios across decisions, including process-crash/event-loss, unscanned→required copy, destination policy, tenant/scope, concurrent metadata vs content, scanner failure, signed URL permanence.
5. Which repairs already recorded for P3 need revision; minimal portable design now vs explicitly later features. Explain if durable scan dispatch or storage-layer URL enforcement must be prerequisites instead of falsely claiming them solved.
6. Open choices only genuinely requiring owner product preference; recommend a coherent package default without claiming an 'ideal' universally best system.
7. Primary URLs with exact section/version/verification limits. No long quotations. If no published evidence exists say so.
Bound the answer to roughly 3500–5000 Russian words; prioritize accurate sources and actionable contracts over number of citations.

sections.title: Уточнение пропавших matrices и сценариев
sections.text: Уточнение к независимому исследованию Vaulter PHP8.4/Laravel12–13 file+CAS+revision+tenant/profile system. В Deep Research ответе пропали содержимое таблиц и acceptance сценарии при выгрузке. Ответь ТОЛЬКО простыми нумерованными списками, без таблиц/кодовых блоков, 1500–2200 слов. Нужны (1) access matrix словами для unscanned/not_required,pending,clean,infected,failed при off,new_content_only,all_content; legacy grandfathering явно зафиксирован, не произвольный timestamp; off не разрешает known infected; fresh optional background rescan failure не уничтожает ещё принимаемый clean evidence; (2) copy/restore: source not_required→required destination, clean evidence same bytes vs changed scanner/scope/tenant; trash restore vs creating new revision; (3) 12 конкретных adversarial cases по durable scan work (commit→publish crash, expired lease/late result), signed URL fresh request after revoke vs in-flight download, system scanner internal read vs публичный bypass, root expectedSequence vs changed descendant и conditional read ETag+304 after revoked auth. (4) Проверь и дай первичные источники отдельно по D27 IAM explicit denies/SCP service-linked exceptions/Cedar и D28 GCS generation+metageneration/Azure If-Match/RFC9110 strong vs node counter. Отдельно: есть ли опубликованное основание требовать BIGINT вместо portable uint32 в Vaulter, или это лишь выбор по throughput/lifetime? Нельзя выдавать предпочтение исследователя за обязательное требование стандарта. existing P3 spec unsignedInteger default0 нельзя менять только 'потому что у Google большое число'. Все свои проекты решений обозначай рекомендациями, а не фактами Google internals. Достоверность tags/необходимость восстановления потерянного scan dispatch проверять по AWS/Azure official. Sources URLs рядом с claims. Это только исследование; не принимать решения и не изменять код.

sections.title: Короткая сверка ordering/durability и integer portability
sections.text: Дай краткий самостоятельный ответ максимум 450 слов по двум спорным утверждениям, с 4–6 прямыми ссылками первичных источников рядом с тезисами, без таблиц. 1) Что именно гарантирует Laravel13 afterCommit()/after_commit и решает ли оно потерю job при crash после DB commit, до queue publish? Отличить ordering/idempotency от durable dispatch; подтверждение transactional outbox — AWS official guidance. 2) Vaulter использует PHP8.4 64bit+PG/MySQL и планирует unsignedInteger sequence default0. Google Cloud Storage generation и Azure ETag доказывают need CAS, но требуют ли они BIGINT для нашего собственного node counter? PostgreSQL integer32 signed, MySQL integer32 unsigned; Laravel PostgresGrammar не поддерживает unsigned modifier. Как корректно определить общий домен, overflow behavior и выбор int32 vs bigint64 без выдуманного обязательного стандарта? RFC9110 strong ETag полный JSON с динамическими ACL/scan полями отдельно от command-visible node sequence. Это research, не implementation.

provenance.note: Owner-requested research/handoff only; design changes deferred to next session. Existing 27 inputs and open decisions unchanged; no product execution or audit verdict.
